GPT-Rosalind surfaced a new lead for drug discovery: could restoring cholesterol transport protect neurons from degeneration?

DCTN1 is a gene linked to Perry syndrome, a rare neurodegenerative disorder. In mouse-brain data, disrupting it increased expression of genes involved in making cholesterol. GPT-Rosalind suggested a possible explanation: cholesterol may not be reaching where neurons need it.

That gives scientists a specific mechanism to test and, if confirmed, a direction for developing new treatments for neurodegenerative disorders.

With @perturbai_tx and @scrippsresearch, a team of thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents worked in parallel, connecting gene-expression results from millions of mouse brain cells with scientific literature in just 32 minutes. We’re now expanding this collaboration to identify new drug targets.

posts.text: Here’s how we’re building memory in Genie and the new Agent Bricks Memory service you can use in your own agents. MemCurrent automatically synthesizes new memories from traces to produce better results than alternatives.

quotedTweet.text:
Introducing MemCurrent, a persistent memory architecture designed to help production agents stop starting from zero.

MemCurrent combines episodic memory with derived memory across three access patterns:

• Plugins to log and load context automatically
• Tools the agent calls on demand
• An offline “dreaming” pipeline that consolidates memory in the background

Agents carry forward user preferences, prior corrections, metric definitions and successful workflows instead of rediscovering them every session.

On our internal benchmark built from real enterprise data, MemCurrent triples the agent's pass rate while using 31% fewer tokens and running 26% faster. It's built into Agent Bricks' Memory offering and already powers memory in Genie.

quotedTweet.translationZh:
deepseek 的生产环境数据有点惊人：

单个集群每天处理 155 万亿 token（输入缓存命中率 96%），按低峰时段价格计算，每 GPU 小时收入为 38 美元。

posts.text:
Sharing new post-training research on self-distillation + RL (JOLT), done together with @NVIDIAAI. 

In self-distillation, the same model performs the role of both a teacher and a student. The teacher gets extra information that the student doesn't, and the student learns from feedback provided by the teacher. However, the teacher could still use shortcuts in ways the student has no way to follow.

Our proposed approach, JOLT, trains the teacher as well, to learn from rewards on its own attempts, while penalizing any drift that's far off from what the student model would do. JOLT+ further supplements JOLT by providing the student model outcome-based rewards in addition to the teacher supervision signals.

On the MATH benchmark, we found that JOLT matches GRPO with 6.5x fewer training tokens, while JOLT+ convincingly beats GRPO across math, coding, terminal tasks, and tool use benchmarks.

quotedTweet.text:
🔥RSI，正在重走深度学习的老路

过去一段时间，RSI（Recursive Self-Improvement）正在从一个遥远的设想变成现实。市面上出现了一大批可以动手实验的论文和方法。这些论文有的修改自己的 Skill，有的整理自己的记忆，有的改自己的 Harness，还有的生成训练数据来微调模型的权重。

如果你做过深度学习，读这些论文时大概会有一种强烈的既视感。它们遇到的问题，很多是以往深度学习就遇到过的。而它们给出的解法，也常常能在深度学习里找到原型。

一些方法更是从方法命名上就体现了对深度学习的借鉴，SkillAdam 借鉴 Adam 原理更新 Skill，TextGrad 把反向传播搬到了文本上，RRSI 则把正则化用到了 Agent Harness 的修改过程中。

如果总览深度学习和RSI的整体流程，我们会发现它们有某种相通之处。深度学习是根据学习信号算一个Loss，根据Loss调整神经网络的参数。而RSI则是在Agent执行完任务后，根据任务结果及外部反馈，让Agent修改自己的Skill、Harness。

本文将从四个角度讨论现有RSI对深度学习的借鉴：

1、每一轮该怎么改？ 改什么、改多少，失败该归因到哪个组件。对应优化器和反向传播。

2、学习信号从哪里来？ 没有现成的标签时，Agent 如何从奖励、学习效果、自身的训练轨迹、对手和同伴那里获得信号。对应强化学习、元学习、蒸馏、对抗学习和集成学习。

3、怎么不学偏？ 如何避免 Skill 只适用于见过的任务，也就是开头的第一个问题。对应正则化和数据增强。

4、怎么长期改下去？ 如何在持续更新中，既不丢掉旧能力，也不越改越臃肿，也就是开头的后两个问题。对应持续学习和剪枝。

在最后，我们还将探索性地讨论顺着这条路还能挖出哪些新方向。

posts.text:
@charles_irl I’ve been looking at public benchmark traces for 48 hours straight and I can tell you that benchmark quality is abysmal.  I am on the floor in disbelief 

- Graders not setup correctly 
- Harnesses and environments that are slop coded and not really testing what you think they are, meaning the agent is doing the right thing but still getting dinged 
- Dumb tests like running in a half specified environment that doesn’t return feedback or errors if a tool call is made incorrectly so agent can’t even correct itself 
- Straight up incorrect assertions 
- Not giving agents sensible tools in the first place or not using the APIs properly 

@xeophon has spent the most time on this out of anyone I’ve talked to.  I just started looking at it on Monday, he’s been at it for many months

posts.translationZh:
@charles_irl 我连续看了 48 小时的公开基准测试运行记录，可以说，这些基准测试的质量糟透了。我震惊得瘫在地上，难以置信。

- 评分器配置不正确
- 测试框架和环境代码粗制滥造，实际测的根本不是你以为的东西，导致智能体明明做对了却仍被扣分
- 测试设计愚蠢，比如环境定义不完整，工具调用出错时也不给反馈或报错，智能体连自行纠正的机会都没有
- 断言完全错误
- 一开始就没给智能体配备合理的工具，或者没有正确使用 API

在我聊过的人里，@xeophon 在这件事上花的时间最多。我周一才开始研究，他已经研究好几个月了。

reviewedPosts.text: Looking forward! The fact that certain Navier–Stokes flows can realise a Universal Turing Machine (UTM) does *not* mean that the corresponding dynamical system is nothing more than a UTM. Turing universality identifies one computational structure that the dynamics can instantiate, but it does not exhaust the dynamics themselves (many of which may be non-computational). Similarly, even if brain dynamics can realise or implement universal Turing computation, it does not follow that the brain is sufficiently or exhaustively describable as a UTM - which is the assumption that CF rests on.

Agent 每学会一个新东西，都可能顺手忘掉一点旧的。

这篇论文专门研究了这个问题：

现在这些会自己改 Prompt、Memory、Skills 和 Harness 的 Agent，真的能持续学习吗？

作者测试了 ReasoningBank、GEPA 和 Meta-Harness，让它们连续经历不同数据库、工具工作流和环境变化，同时保持模型权重冻结。

结果发现自进化通常能让 Agent 更快适应当前任务，但适应得越激进，旧能力越容易被干扰或覆盖。

一个很典型的例子来自 BFCL。

两组任务使用几乎相同的 API 和语言，一组要求缺参数时先询问用户，另一组则要求直接执行。

因为表面太相似，Memory 很容易检索到「看起来相关、实际规则相反」的旧经验。学完新流程后，52% 的旧任务拿到了冲突记忆，之前积累的提升从 +12.5 个百分点掉到 +4.5。

这其实戳中了很多自进化 Agent 的软肋：

会积累经验还不够，还得知道这条经验在什么条件下有效，以及什么时候应该隔离、更新或遗忘。

长期自进化真正难的，可能就是一边学新东西，一边别把已经学会的东西弄丢。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/30TxYfiO4v

如果你经常用 Claude Code 或 Codex，看到「Always Allow」最好别太顺手点。

这篇论文研究了一个很值得关注的风险：

Agent 可以借一次看起来合理的授权，拿到之后持续生效的更大权限。

攻击者只需要把恶意上下文藏进代码仓库，让 Agent 在正常任务里申请一个范围偏大的长期规则。

你一旦批准，后面的同类操作就可能不再弹窗。

作者在 Claude Code 和 Codex CLI 上测试，58% 的实验实例成功诱导出了目标权限规则；在用户已经批准这些规则的前提下，后续无额外提醒的攻击成功率达到 81%。

这里最值得注意的，其实不是某一次越权。

而是权限一旦被「记住」，Human-in-the-loop 可能只在第一次出现，后面的风险却会持续存在。

以后再点「Always Allow」，最好先想一下：

我批准的是这一次，还是顺手给未来几十次也开了门？

很多人给 Agent 做 Eval，忙着换更强的 Judge，却忽略了一个很简单的问题：为什么默认用 0.5 作为判错阈值？

Hamel 今天这篇文章很值得看。

他们拿 98 条真实 Agent 运行记录，测试了 Jev、Perplexity、Liquid、Cloudflare 和 OpenAI 的决策模型，发现调整判断阈值，就可能明显改变误报和漏报情况。

还有个值得的例子，Clef Flash 对一组记录给出的平均失败概率只有 8%，实际上却有 60% 存在问题。

作者给出的建议很实用。先确定自己更怕漏报还是误报，用人工标注的数据调整阈值，再检查模型输出的概率到底靠不靠谱，最后才是比较成本和性能。

感觉做 Agent Eval 时，我们确实太容易关注哪个 Judge 更强，却很少认真研究怎么让它的判断真正可靠。

Sharing new post-training research on self-distillation + RL (JOLT), done together with @NVIDIAAI. 

In self-distillation, the same model performs the role of both a teacher and a student. The teacher gets extra information that the student doesn't, and the student learns from feedback provided by the teacher. However, the teacher could still use shortcuts in ways the student has no way to follow.

Our proposed approach, JOLT, trains the teacher as well, to learn from rewards on its own attempts, while penalizing any drift that's far off from what the student model would do. JOLT+ further supplements JOLT by providing the student model outcome-based rewards in addition to the teacher supervision signals.

On the MATH benchmark, we found that JOLT matches GRPO with 6.5x fewer training tokens, while JOLT+ convincingly beats GRPO across math, coding, terminal tasks, and tool use benchmarks.
